# Smallest Stable Index I.

@example The cuts have gaps 4, 4, 3, 3 and 0. The first gap of at most 3 is at position 2, where it equals k.
[6,2,8,5,9]
3
=> 2

@example Every cut has the left maximum 10 and the right minimum 3, a gap of 7.
[10,7,3]
6
=> -1

@example The gaps are 3, 3, 0, 3 and 3: only the cut at 2 has a gap of 0.
[4,1,5,9,6]
0
=> 2

# A single number is always stable.
[7]
0
=> 0

# Never falling: every gap is 0.
[1,1,2,3]
0
=> 0

# Falling: every gap is 9 - 1 = 8. A gap equal to k counts.
[9,6,4,1]
7
=> -1

[9,6,4,1]
8
=> 0

# The gaps are 1, 8, 8 and 0: the first stable cut is wanted, not the last.
[1,8,0,9]
1
=> 0

# Only the last cut is stable.
[1,8,0,9]
0
=> 3

# The gaps are 3, 3, 0, 3, 3 and 0: the stable cuts are not all at the end.
[4,1,5,9,6,10]
0
=> 2

# The right piece includes nums[i]: at position 1 the gap is 7 - 3 = 4,
# not 7 - 8.
[7,3,8]
1
=> 2

# The largest values and gaps.
[1000000000,0]
999999999
=> -1

[1000000000,0]
1000000000
=> 0

# Large numbers: only the last cut, at the largest value, has a gap of 0.
[700000000,1000000000,600000000,1000000000]
0
=> 3

# Numbers far above 10^6, which a small starting minimum would hide.
[500000000,700000000]
0
=> 0

# Random small cases from gen.c (lc check --regen makes them).
@gen 1 small
[3,7,0,9,9,9,3]
7
=> 0

@gen 2 small
[999999999,999999997,999999995,999999997,999999999]
0
=> 4

@gen 3 small
[999999997,999999993,999999994,999999997,999999992,999999993,999999991,1000000000]
3
=> 7

@gen 4 small
[1,4,0,8]
0
=> 3

@gen 5 small
[2,9,9,4,3,1]
8
=> 0

@gen 6 small
[6,1]
4
=> -1

@gen 7 small
[5,0,4,6,2,4]
3
=> 2

@gen 8 small
[999999995,1000000000,999999993,999999996,999999995,999999992,999999992]
7
=> 0
